parole.significato: active, effective, practical, put into practice, real (given effect or manifested in reality by means of action)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἔμπρακτος (émpraktos, “within one's power to do”) with semantic loan from German tatsächlich.
Learned borrowing from German Enzym (in its new meaning) from Byzantine Greek ἔνζυμον a substantivized neuter from the adjective ἔνζυμος (énzumos), formed from the ancient ἐν + ζύμη (zúmē, “leaven”).

Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἀγκυλωτός (ankulōtós), from stem ἀγκυλω- of verb ἀγκυλόω (ankulóō, “crook, bend”) with ending -τός (-tós), from ἀγκύλος (ankúlos, “curved”). Semantic loan from German Hakenkreuz.
αίτιος (aítios, “causative”) + -ότητα (-ótita, “-ity, -ness”), calque of German Kausalität. First attested 1834.
Ultimately from German Akkordeon.
Learned formation from αλκοόλ (alkoól) + -ούχος (-oúchos), a calque of German alkoolhaltig.
Borrowed from German Allergie. Coined by Austrian pediatrician Clemens von Pirquet in 1906 from Ancient Greek ἄλλος (állos, “other”) + ἔργον (érgon, “work, activity”), on the model of Energie.

parole.significato: coffee bar, milk bar, etc (outlet for soft drinks, coffee, ice cream, etc.)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἀναψυκτήριον (anapsuktḗrion, “recreational place”), from the past stem ἀναψυκ- (anapsuk-) of ἀναψύχω (anapsúkhō, “to cool, refresh”) + -τήριον (-tḗrion), with semantic loan from German Εrfrischungsraum.

parole.significato: reborrowing for which see the term αναδανεισμός (anadaneismós)
parole.testo: αντι- (anti-, “counter”) + δάνειο (dáneio, “loan, borrowing”). Already in Katharevousa as ἀντιδάνειον. A rendering or calque of German Rückwanderer.
αντι- (anti-, “anti-, un-”) + ποίηση (poíisi, “poetry”) + -ικός (-ikós, “-ic”), calque of German unpoetisch. First attested 1892.
αντι- (anti-) + πρυτανεία (prytaneía), calque of German Ρrorektorat

parole.significato: prorector, dean (holder of office in institution)
parole.testo: αντι- (anti-) + πρύτανης (prýtanis), calque of German Ρrorektor
Learnedly from αρχαιο- (archaio-) + -γνωσία (-gnosía), a calque of German Altertumskunde.
Learnedly from αυτο- (afto-) + νοητ(ός) (noït(ós)) + -ος (-os), a calque of German selbstverständlich. Compare Koine Greek αὐτονόητος (autonóētos, “exclusively conceptual”).
Learnedly from Ancient Greek βι(ῶ) (bi(ô)) + -ώνω (-óno), with semantic loan from German erleben.
Borrowed from German Wolfram.

parole.significato: rainfall (the occurrence of liquid precipitation, the fall of rain)
parole.testo: Learnedly from βροχή (vrochí, “rain”) + -ό- (-ó-) + πτώση (ptósi, “fall”) , a calque of German Regenfall.

parole.significato: Yot, the uncommon Greek letter ϳ.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Jot (“the letter J”).
Learnedly from γνωστ(ός) (gnost(ós)) + -ο- (-o-) + -ποιώ (-poió), with semantic loan from German bekanntmachen.

parole.significato: silviculture, forestry (the art and practice of cultivating, exploiting and renewing forests for commercial purposes)
parole.testo: From δασοπόν(ος) (dasopón(os)) + -ία (-ía), a calque of German Forstwirtschaft. First attested in 1891.

From δημο- (dimo-, “demo-”) + -σκόπηση (-skópisi, “-scopy”) or a learned borrowing from German Demoskopie. See δήμος m (dímos, “municipality, community”) & σκοπός m (skopós, “goal”). A word creation with Greek combining forms to replace the loanword γκάλοπ n (gkálop, “Gallup poll”). The initial sens
From Ancient Greek δημοτικός, from δημότης (dēmótēs), from δῆμος (dêmos, “country, land”). For music, songs: calque of German Volkslieder.

parole.significato: dissemination, spreading, transmission (of ideas, messages, news, trends, etc.)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek διάδοσις (diádosis, “distribution”), with -ση (-si) ending and semantic loan from German Verbreitung (von Gerüchten) and English spreading (of rumours) in the sense 'rumours'.
Learnedly from διαφωτίζω (diafotízo) + -μός (-mós), a calque of German Aufklärung.
Substantivised feminine of the adjective διδακτικός (didaktikós), from the Hellenistic διδακτικός (didaktikós). Semantic loan from German Didaktik, itself from διδακτικός (didaktikós).

From Ancient Greek εἶναι (eînai), present infinitive of εἰμί (eimí, “I am”). * (For the noun): Semantic loan from German Sein. * (For the 3rd person of verb) According to Babiniotis, not from the infinitive εἶναι (eînai), but from the Byzantine Greek ἔναι (énai) < Ancient Greek ἔνι (éni), a short fo
From Ancient Greek ἐκκρούω. For sense in linguistics, a semantic loan from German ausstoßen. Morphologically, from εκ- (“counter-”) + κρούω (“strike”).
Univerbation of the Katharevousa phrase ἐν τάξει (en táxei), modelled after Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) τάξει (táxei, “order”), the latter a dative form of τάξις (táxis). Calque of German in Ordnung.
From εξω- (exo-) + στρέφ(ω) (stréf(o)) + -ής (-ís), a calque of German extravertiert.
Learnedly from επι- (epi-) + δειν(ός) (dein(ós)) + -ώνω (-óno), a calque of German verschlechtern.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐπιδρῶ (epidrô, “to do extra”), with semantic loan from German einwirken, auswirken. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + δρω (dro).
Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἐργοδότης (ergodótēs), Semantic loan from German Arbeitgeber. By surface analysis, εργο- (ergo-, “work”) + -δότης (-dótis, “giver”)
From εσω- (eso-) + στρέφ(ω) (stréf(o)) + -ής (-ís), a calque of German introvertiert.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek εὕρημα (heúrēma) with semantic loan from German Befund and English findings.

From German Zirkon (“zircon mineral”) via French zircon, formed in the 1780s from Arabic زَرْقُون (zarqūn, “zircon, minium”), from Middle Persian 𐭦𐭫𐭢𐭥𐭭 (zlgʿn /⁠zargōn⁠/), from Classical Persian زرگون (zargōn)/Middle Persian 𐭦𐭫𐭢𐭥𐭭 (zlgʿn /⁠zargōn⁠/, “red lead”), from Proto-Iranian *jr̥Hanyam (“gold”

Calque of German gewillt. Learnedly but erroneously formed as a passive perfect participle of θέλω (thélo), from Ancient Greek ἐθέλω (ethélō) (which has no such participle), by analogy with ημαρτημένος (imartiménos), archaic/learned passive perfect participle of αμαρτάνω (amartáno), from Ancient Gre
From ημί- (imí-) + φως (fos), a calque of German Halblicht and French demi-jour.

parole.significato: mezzanine, entresol, an intermediate floor just above ground level
parole.testo: ημι- (imi-, “semi-, half”) + -ώροφος (-órofos, “floor”), from όροφος m (órofos), a calque of German Halbgeschoß
From German Idealist.
Learned formation from ιδιο- (idio-) + -κτήτης (-ktḗtēs) (compare Koine Greek ἰδιοκτήτωρ (idioktḗtōr)), formed as a calque of German Eigenbesitzer.
Learned formation from ιδιο- (idio-) + -κτησία (-ktēsía), formed as a calque of German Eigenbesitz.

parole.significato: and so forth, and so on
parole.testo: See και (kai, “and”), ούτω (oúto, “so”, archaic adverb) & καθεξής (kathexís, “forth”, archaic adverb). According to Petrounias, a semantic loan from German und so weiter (usw.).

parole.significato: kitsch (of questionable aesthetic value; excessively sentimental, overdone or vulgar)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Kitsch.
From κλίνη (klíni) + -ο- (-o-) + σκέπασμα (sképasma), a calque of German Bettdecke.
From κόσμος (kósmos, “world”) + θεωρία (theoría, “theory”) a calque of German Weltanschauung.

parole.significato: of or related to percussion instruments
parole.testo: From Hellenistic Koine Greek κρουστός, and a semantic loan from German Schlaginstrumente or French instruments à percussion.
Learned borrowing from German Zyklothymie, from Ancient Greek. By surface analysis, κυκλο- (kyklo-) + θυμ(ός) (thym(ós)) + -ία (-ía).
Learnedly from κυκλοθυμ(ία) (kyklothym(ía)) + -ικός (-ikós), a calque of German zyklothym.
From λαός (laós, “people”) + -γραφία (-grafía, “writing about”), calque of German Volkskunde. Modern sense has completely replaced the Koine Greek sense of "census".
Learnedly from λεπτ(ό) (lept(ó)) + -ο- (-o-) + δείκτης (deíktis), a calque of German Minutenzeiger.
Learned borrowing from German Lux, from Latin lux (“light”).
From German Lumpen.
From Ancient Greek μέσῳ (mésōi), dative singular of μέσος (mésos, “middle”), a semantic loan from German mittels.

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek μετάθεσις (metáthesis, “change of position”) with, in the sense 'transfer', semantic loan from German Versetzung and French déplacement. By surface analysis, μεταθέτω (metathéto) + -ση (-si).
μεταρρυθμ- (metarrythm-, “to reform”) + -ιστής (-istís, “-ist, -er”), religious term is a calque of German Reformator. First attested 1871.

parole.significato: forget-me-not (small 5-petalled blue flower from the genus Myosotis)
parole.testo: Calque of German Vergissmeinnicht.
Borrowed from German Nazi.
Borrowed from German Nazismus.
From German Nazist.
Borrowed from German Ninhydrin, suffixed with -ίνη (-íni, “-ine”).
Learnedly from νομο- (nomo-) + σχέδιο (schédio), a calque of German Gesetzentwurf.
From German Determinismus.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek νόημα (nóēma, “thought, perception, understanding”), with semantic loan from German Noem, itself from the Ancient Greek term, and Wink (“sign, wave”).
From οδοντ- (odont-, “tooth”) + ιατρός (iatrós, “doctor”), a calque of German Zahnarzt.
Learned borrowing from German Ökologie or French écologie. By surface analysis, οικο- (oiko-) + -λογία (-logía).
Learned borrowing from German ökologisch and French écologique. By surface analysis, οικολογία (oikología) + -ικός (-ikós).

parole.significato: homosexual, gay (attracted to the same sex)
parole.testo: Back-formation from ομοφυλοφιλ(ία) (omofylofil(ía)) + -ος (-os). By surface analysis, ομο- (omo-, “same, homo-”) + φύλο (fýlo, “gender, sex”) + -φιλος (-filos, “-friend, -phile”), calque of German homosexuell.
Nominalized learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp”) with semantic loan from German Säure and French acide.
Learnedly from πάγ(ος) (pág(os)) + -ο- (-o-) + -δρόμος (-drómos), a calque of German Eisläufer.
From παρ- (par-) + ενέργεια (enérgeia, “action”), calque of German Nebenwirkung.

parole.significato: folk etymology (false etymology that incorrectly explains the origin of a word)
parole.testo: From παρ- (par-) + ετυμολογία (etymología), calque of German Volksetymologie. First attested 1874.
Learnedly from παχύ- (pachý-) + ρευστ(ός) (refst(ós)) + -ος (-os), a calque of German dickflüssig.

parole.significato: footpath, footway, pavement (UK), sidewalk (US) (a paved path, for the use of pedestrians, located at the side of a roa…
parole.testo: Learnedly, from πεζο- (pezo-) + δρόμος (drómos) + -ιον (-ion), formed as a calque of German Fußgängerweg (“pedestrian path”).
From German Polygraph.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek προσγρᾰ́φω. Also, semantic loan from German zuschreiben. Morphologically, from προσ- (“toward”) + γράφω (“write”).
From German Swastika, from Sanskrit स्वस्तिक (svástika).
Semantic loan from German Lehnübersetzung and French emprunt. Also see μεταφραστικό δάνειο (metaphrastikó dáneio, “translation loan”).

parole.significato: rail (the metal bar forming part of the track for a railroad)
parole.testo: From σιδηρο- (sidiro-) + τροχιά (trochiá), a calque of German Eisenbahn.
Learnedly from the σπουδασ- stem of σπουδάζω (spoudázo) + -τήριο (-tírio), a loose calque of German Studierzimmer.

parole.significato: to coordinate, effect by concerted or joint effort
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek σῠντονίᾱ (sŭntoníā, “harmony (of sounds; (ancient) intensity”) + -ίζω (-ízo), with semantic loan from German abstimmen (“(reflexive) to synchronize”). For the "syntonize" meaning, reborrowing and semantic loan from French syntoniser.
σύρμα (sýrma, “wire”) + σχοινί (schoiní, “rope”), calque of German Drahtseil
τιμή (timí, “price”) + -ο- (-o-) + λόγος (lógos, “computation, reckoning”), calque of German Preiskurant. First attested 1856.

parole.significato: quotation, citation (a fragment of a human expression that is repeated by somebody else)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from German Zitat with -ο (-o) ending, from Latin citātus.
From ύπαρξη (ýparxi, “existence”) + -ισμός (-ismós, “-ism”), calque of German Existentialismus.
Calque of German Schlafzimmer. By surface analysis, ύπν(ος) (ýpn(os), “sleep”) + -ο- (-o-) + δωμάτιο (domátio, “room”).
Learnedly from φιλ- (fil-) + -άρεσκος (-áreskos) (from αρέσκω (arésko)), modelled on αυτάρεσκος (aftáreskos). A calque of German gefallsüchtig.

Borrowed from German Futter in its second sense (“lining”). This meaning is preserved in the doublet φόδρα (fódra), which entered the language via Venetan fodra, itself a borrowing tracing back to Proto-Germanic *fōdrą (“sheath”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, guard”).

parole.significato: flare (firework that produces a brilliant light or intense heat without an explosion)
parole.testo: From φωτο- (foto-, “light”) + βολίδα (volída, “missile, projectile”), calque of German Leuchtkugel. First attested 1887.
From χειρο- (cheiro-, “hand”) + βομβίδα (vomvída, “grenade”), a calque of German Handgranate.
Learnedly from χιόνι (chióni, “snow”) + -ό- (-ó-) + πτώση (ptósi, “fall”), a calque of German Schneefall.

parole.significato: safe, coffer, strongbox (box, usually made of metal, in which valuables can be locked for safekeeping)
parole.testo: Learnedly from χρηματο- (chrimato-, “money”) + κιβώτιο (kivótio, “box, casket, ark”), calque of German Geldschrank. First attested 1868.
From ψυχ- (psych-, “psych-, soul”) + ανάλυση (análysi, “analysis”), learned borrowing from German Psychoanalyse or from French psychanalyse.
